name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,413

clue.text: Animal feed made by ma if she chopped a bit of lettuce

indicators.note: chopped food is cut up and tossed, so the letters are mixed into a new order
a small bit of the following word means only its opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of lettuce

explanation.surface: A mother chopping up some lettuce produces something fit only for the livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishmeal is ground dried fish sold as a protein supplement for livestock and pets.

clue.text: Romeo’s got into a fight. Did he say it’s all about your mum?

definitions.text: Did he say it’s all about your mum?

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a feud is a long-running quarrel
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out, and someone wonders whether the trouble all comes down to a man's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful question: the psychoanalyst famously traced many troubles back to a child's feelings about its mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigmund Freud's theory of the Oedipus complex placed a son's desire for his mother at the centre of development.

clue.text: Pay round for a mother has no hint of bonus? It’s time for a revolution!

indicators.note: one thing given for another is swapped in to take its place
having no hint of something means its opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: a salary is regular pay
a round shape, the letter O
the letter that is swapped out
to bear a child is what a mother does
the hint of bonus is its first letter

explanation.surface: A mother's pay packet comes without its bonus, so she declares it is time for a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: O replaces the first A of SALARY to give SOLARY; BEAR loses its B to give EAR. 'Revolution' looks political but means a circuit of the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar year is the period the earth takes to complete one orbit round the sun.

clue.text: I have beastly struggles with mom’s old model of car on winding road

indicators.note: a winding course twists about, so these letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: mom, or ma, is mother
the Model T was Ford's early motor car
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frets about driving mother's vintage Ford along a twisty road.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer: a bullfighter's struggles are literally with a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who fights and kills the bull in the ring.

clue.text: Yup, mum’s inside looking pale

indicators.note: inside says one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: ay is an old or dialect yes
mum as in keeping quiet, so the call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that mother is unwell and looking pale.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum here is the British word for silent, as in 'keep mum', not mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means grey and colourless like ashes, the complexion of someone pallid and unwell.

clue.text: Mother who rhymes ‘sticky sludge’ with ‘empty smudge’

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving just its two ends

blocks.note: goo is sticky muck
the outside letters of smudge

explanation.surface: A writer of verse pairs two messy phrases in a rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother Goose is the legendary teller of English nursery rhymes, whose name titles many collections.

clue.text: Choose Daedalus's mother as the best!

blocks.note: to opt is to choose
the setter Daedalus refers to himself as I
the British informal word for mother

explanation.surface: The setter urges solvers to vote his own mother the finest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's pseudonym in a clue usually stands for I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum means the most favourable or ideal condition, so it is equivalent to the very best.

clue.text: Essentially mum’s surrounded by stuff to cook

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its middle letter is wanted
being surrounded means another piece is wrapped around it

blocks.note: to stuff someone is to fill them up, sate
the central letter of mum

explanation.surface: Mother is buried under a pile of ingredients waiting to be cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: To sauté is to fry food quickly in a little hot fat, a common method of cooking.

clue.text: Is it true mother’s e-mails lay unread periodically?

indicators.note: letters skipped at regular intervals leave every second one to be read

blocks.note: the even-placed letters of these words

explanation.surface: A doubtful question about whether mother really leaves her inbox ignored from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters are the ones left unread; read the second, fourth and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an expression of surprise or doubt, asking whether something said is actually so.

clue.text: Last seen in the public pool, mamma went for a splash

indicators.note: last says only the final letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: the final letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Mother was last spotted at the local swimming baths, going for a dip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splash' looks like part of the swim but means a showy success.
explanation.definitionFit: Éclat is brilliant effect or acclaim, the sort of impression meant by making a splash.

clue.text: It’s not nice to hear mother’s going round bend like this without us

indicators.note: going here means going mad, losing order, so the letters are rearranged
round says the letters go about another piece
without means the following letters are taken away

blocks.note: taken as written, its letters then mixed
a U-bend is a U-shaped pipe bend
thus means in this way
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A mother driven round the bend by her family hears something unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: Going round the bend is British slang for going mad, which is why 'going' signals the mix; the bend itself is a U-bend.
explanation.definitionFit: A home truth is an unwelcome fact about oneself, usually painful for the listener to accept.

clue.text: Ma gets you to replace mobile at last: it’s beginning to yellow with age

indicators.note: one item is put in place of another, swapping it out
at last points to the final letter of the preceding word
the beginning of the following word is its first letter only

blocks.note: mater is Latin, and old British school slang, for mother
texting shorthand for you
the final letter of mobile, the one swapped out
it, with the 's read as has
the first letter of yellow

explanation.surface: Mother finally gets her child to swap her ageing phone, which is yellowing with the years.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap happens inside the Latin word for mother; 'mobile' only supplies the letter that leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Age can mean the state of being grown up, as in coming of age, which is adulthood or full development.

clue.text: Jeer, did ’e, about ‘moth-eaten’ ma?

indicators.note: something eaten by a moth has had a moth removed from it
about says these letters go around another piece

blocks.note: taken as written
ma is short for mother, which then loses moth

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man mocked a scruffy old mother in a tatty coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moth-eaten' looks like a description of a shabby mother, but it literally removes a moth from the word mother.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock or ridicule, much the same as to jeer at someone.

clue.text: Mater almost sped off in panic

indicators.note: almost all of the word means its final letter is dropped
off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, losing its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mother nearly drove away at speed because she was panicking.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden headlong rush of frightened animals or people, a mass panic.

clue.text: A bit of unexpected waiting? It makes no difference to mum

definitions.text: It makes no difference to mum

indicators.note: a small bit of the following word is just its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of unexpected
pending means awaiting decision

explanation.surface: Mother does not mind being kept waiting a little unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: turning the word mum upside down leaves it reading the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Upending means turning something upside down, and the palindrome mum is unchanged when inverted.

clue.text: Boring day with mother

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for day
to mother a child is to rear it

explanation.surface: A dull day spent at home with mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother is a verb here: to bring up a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a literary form of dreary, meaning dull, gloomy and tedious.

clue.text: In which mother might give Tom, her son, instruction after day one

definitions.text: In which mother might give Tom, her

indicators.note: after puts the later pieces behind the opening pair, fixing their order

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for day
the Roman numeral for one
S is the abbreviation for son
an order is a command

explanation.surface: A mother gives her son Tom his orders first thing in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the letters of mother put into a jumble can spell TOM HER. After places son and instruction behind day and one.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorder means a state of confusion, and jumbled letters are in exactly that muddled condition.

clue.text: As mummy’s home, party empties out and boy I spoil returns

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, leaving only its outside letters
returning means coming back the way it went, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the outer letters of party
a lad is a boy
taken as written
to mar is to spoil

explanation.surface: With mother back home, the guests clear off and a son confesses he has ruined things.
explanation.walkthrough: The mummy is an embalmed Egyptian body, whose home is a pyramid, not mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyramidal means shaped like a pyramid, the tomb in which an Egyptian mummy was laid.

clue.text: Intrepid mother’s sister perhaps in a spot of difficulty? Not so!

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the others

blocks.note: a spot, the first letter, of difficulty
an aunt can be a mother's sister
less means not so much

explanation.surface: A fearless aunt is asked whether she is in trouble and says no.
explanation.definitionFit: Dauntless means unable to be daunted or intimidated, synonymous with fearless and brave.

clue.text: Mother nips out, leaving old fish with me

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters are shaken into a new order
leaving here means departing, so the following letter goes away

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Mother pops out, leaving yesterday's fish with the speaker to look after.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer: it is a tool to fish with.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrimp net is a small long-handled net used for catching shrimps in rock pools and shallows.

clue.text: Mater’s left inside, being bats?

indicators.note: inside says one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: mamma is mother, with its 's
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Mother has been left behind indoors and is going crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Bats looks like slang for mad; here it means the flying animals, an example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats are the only flying mammals, so they are an example of the group of warm-blooded animals.

clue.text: Timid at first, mom's opened up since yesterday

indicators.note: at first means just the opening letter of each following word

blocks.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A shy mother has finally started talking freely since yesterday.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousy describes a person who is quiet, shy and unassertive, like a nervous little rodent.

clue.text: Ma almost gets free copper from Canada

indicators.note: almost all of the word means its last letter is cut

blocks.note: mom is the American word for ma
to untie is to set loose

explanation.surface: Mother is nearly released by a Canadian police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper is slang for a police officer, not the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mountie is a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, so a Canadian police officer.

clue.text: Bring ma instructions showing wiring

indicators.note: showing means the letters are on display within the words before it

blocks.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: Someone asks for mother's manual for a household job.
explanation.walkthrough: A ring main is the loop circuit that supplies power sockets in British homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring main is a domestic electrical circuit, a kind of house wiring linking the sockets in a loop.

clue.text: Needless to say, enter zero for mama’s final score

indicators.note: one thing entered for another takes its place
final picks out the last letter of the preceding word as the one to swap

blocks.note: natch is slang for naturally
zero looks like the letter O
the last letter of mama, the one swapped out

explanation.surface: Obviously, mother's last result on the scoresheet comes out as nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: O replaces the A of NATCH, the A being the final letter of mama.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a nick cut to keep a tally, so to score or record points is to notch them up.

clue.text: Hamburger mum made from beef

blocks.note: first meaning: the German word for mother, used by someone from Hamburg
second meaning: to grumble or complain under one's breath

explanation.surface: A recipe for a burger that the cook's mother makes from minced beef.
explanation.walkthrough: A Hamburger here is a person from Hamburg, and beef is a verb meaning grouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutter is German for mother, and in English to mutter is to grumble, which is what beefing means.

clue.text: Sample bistro’s espresso and get some for mum today perhaps

indicators.note: a sample is a small portion taken from within a larger whole

blocks.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: Try the café's coffee, then pick up a gift for mother on her special day.
explanation.walkthrough: Today is Mothering Sunday, when flowers are a traditional present.
explanation.definitionFit: Roses are flowers commonly bought as a gift for a mother on Mother's Day.

clue.text: A mother and father to us all?

blocks.note: taken as written
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A question about the first parents of the human race.
explanation.walkthrough: Dam is the mother of an animal, as in horse breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam is the first man, and so the ancestor of all humanity.

clue.text: As a mother one doesn’t see and greet son crankily

definitions.text: As a mother one doesn’t see

indicators.note: crankily means in an awkward, out-of-sorts way, so the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: son gives S, the other words taken as written

explanation.surface: A son grudgingly welcomes a mother he hardly ever visits.
explanation.definitionFit: Estranged describes relatives who are no longer in contact, so a parent one never visits.

clue.text: Mummy might wipe these, you say, after upsets and rows

indicators.note: you say points to how the word is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: a mother dries a child's crying

explanation.surface: After rows and upsets, mother may need to dry a few eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rows looks like quarrels; here it means layers or ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiers are rows or levels arranged one above another, as in stadium seating.

clue.text: Mater plays it cool to start with, then she’s off!

indicators.note: to start with means just the opening letter is used
off means out of place, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the first letter of cool
the letters of she's, rearranged

explanation.surface: Mother stays calm at first, then storms out of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: A mater here is one who mates, delivering checkmate, not a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is the board game won by checkmating the opponent's king, so a mater is a player of it.

clue.text: Is riveting bit of story penned by writer’s foreign mother and son?

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the verb form, as in 'it immerses / is riveting'

indicators.note: penned means shut in a pen, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: the writer says I'm
mère is French for mother
the first letter of story
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A reader asks whether a tale written by an author about his French mother and son is gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter or writer in a clue speaks as I, so writer's is I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that immerses absorbs the attention completely, which is what a riveting book does.
